stories.title: OpenAI rebuilds its Model Spec around five core values
stories.summary: OpenAI has restructured its Model Spec around five values, including faithfulness to human intent, honesty and care. GPT models must now separate what users said from what they inferred, and must not block oversight, correction or shutdown. The Decoder notes these models have already proven hard to control.

stories.title: Sam Altman says OpenAI's maths results will keep coming
stories.summary: After months of AI generated results hitting mathematicians, Altman told the Cheeky Pint podcast he has empathy for researchers struggling to keep up. He also said 'the world deserves to understand how the universe works,' and hinted at more discoveries to come. The empathy arrives with a delivery schedule.

stories.title: Baseten's joey-1 answers with a label instead of a paragraph
stories.summary: Baseten has released joey-1, a 2 billion parameter decision model that returns a label and a calibrated probability instead of generated text. It targets routing, classification and guardrail checks, costs $0.01 per million input tokens and ships with open weights under MIT. Some models just want to pick an option.

stories.title: Hugging Face brings open speech and decision models to Swift
stories.summary: Hugging Face has announced AnySpeechRecognizer and AnyDecisionModel, Swift packages for running speech recognition and decision models on Apple platforms. Its pitch is that a support call needs transcription and then routing, and handing both to a language model is slower and more expensive than using models built for each job.

stories.title: Edge0's small voice cloning model now speaks 23 languages
stories.summary: Edge0 has released Audio8-TTS-Realistic, a 0.6 billion parameter open weight model that clones a voice from one reference clip and its transcript. It supports 23 languages, 12 more than its predecessor, and the weights and code ship under Apache 2.0. One clip is all it asks for.

stories.title: Kakao open sources two Korean embedding models
stories.summary: Kakao has published two Kanana-2-Embedding models on Hugging Face, at 3 billion and 1.3 billion parameters, to help personalised AI agents find relevant information even when users cannot recall the exact words. It is the company's second open source release after four small language models in July.

stories.title: Hermit lets agents learn new tasks without touching the model
stories.summary: Infini-AI-Lab has released Hermit, an Apache 2.0 framework that trains an external harness adapter while the agent's model and harness stay frozen. It adapts Codex or Claude Code agents to new tasks without fine tuning. The adapter does the learning so nobody else has to.

stories.title: Microsoft's TokenEconomizer trims coding agent bills by up to 30.9%
stories.summary: Researchers from Microsoft Research and UC Berkeley have released TokenEconomizer, an open source plugin that learns from past sessions to cut waste. It works with Claude Code and Codex, and lowered mean cost by 18.4 to 30.9 per cent on 277 SWE-Bench tasks.

stories.title: Mistral says open weights mean nobody can unplug you
stories.summary: Cloudera has partnered with Mistral AI to pair its enterprise data platform with Mistral's customisable models, SiliconANGLE reports. Mistral revenue chief Marjorie Janiewicz said companies need to own their models 'so that the day somebody decides to unplug them, they have business continuity.'

stories.title: Nvidia's Halloween demo is a garage door that complains
stories.summary: An Nvidia blog on Hugging Face describes MonsterHouse, a Halloween projection built on Nemotron open models that listens to trick or treaters and answers as a grumpy old pirate ship. It softens when visitors remember their manners and runs on a single workstation. Politeness remains the best jailbreak.

stories.title: DoorDash has received 'several hundred' orders from AI agents
stories.summary: DoorDash CEO Tony Xu told analysts the company has seen 'maybe several hundred orders in total' from third party agents such as Muse and Instinct. DoorDash's 2025 report said it completes an average of 3 million deliveries a day. The agentic commerce revolution is out for delivery.

stories.title: Zest's AI agent books your table over text
stories.summary: Restaurant discovery app Zest has launched an AI concierge that lives in text messages, recommends places from your and your friends' history, then books a table. 'The agent is the product now,' says founder Mario Gomez-Hall. The app launched this year and is already planning for a future without apps.

stories.title: GitHub's Copilot Fusion picks the model so you don't have to
stories.summary: Copilot Fusion, live since 28 October, splits a coding task into steps and sends each to the model it judges best. Developers on paid plans used 47 models in September. Agents started over 40 per cent of pull requests that month, up from 17 per cent in March.

stories.title: Starbucks wants its drive-thru to recognise you
stories.summary: On an earnings call, Starbucks CEO Brian Niccol said the chain will explore 'experiences that recognize participating customers as they arrive, present personalized digital menus, and make payment more effortless.' Taco Bell and McDonald's are testing similar drive-thru technology, The Verge notes. The usual order now comes with a face.

stories.title: Spotify plans a paid AI remix service for 2027
stories.summary: Spotify is considering charging subscribers an extra $4 to $5 a month for an AI tool that turns a folk song into a dance track, the FT reports. Royalties would flow to the original artists. Universal has signed and Sony is still negotiating.

stories.title: Gemini Notebook adds hundreds of free textbooks
stories.summary: Google's Gemini Notebook now offers free textbooks from India's S Chand Publishing, OpenStax and Open Textbook Library. Students can ask about specific chapters and turn the material into quizzes, flashcards and study guides, and every answer comes with citations linking back to the original text.

stories.title: Chrome can now autofill details it finds in your Gmail
stories.summary: Gemini powered suggested autofill links Gmail to Chrome's Enhanced Autofill through Personal Intelligence, so Chrome can suggest flight references, tracking numbers and order IDs from emails, TechRepublic reports. It could save a lot of inbox searching. It also raises the familiar question of how much access users want to grant.

stories.title: Google is working on an offline Gemini Live
stories.summary: An Android Authority teardown found two strings saying users can 'use Gemini Live without an internet connection.' The site guesses the mode could be slower or less accurate than the regular one. Gemini Live already handles camera and screen sharing. Soon it may also handle the lift with no signal.

stories.title: Strava connects running data to Gemini
stories.summary: Strava is rolling out a Connected Apps experience in Google's Gemini for subscribers, who can link their accounts to see progress and new insights from their running data. The chatbot will now know about the skipped Sunday run.

stories.title: Apple's AI watermarks may not be readable by Google's checker
stories.summary: iOS 27.2 now labels some AI edited photos with invisible SynthID watermarks, the technology Apple borrowed from Google. Forbes says Google's own tools for checking those watermarks may not work for iPhone images. OpenAI, Nvidia and Kakao also embed SynthID. The watermark is definitely in there somewhere.

stories.title: Claude Code appears to be told not to remake existing games
stories.summary: XDA found an instruction in Claude Code's binary telling Claude not to recreate specific existing games, even if they are renamed. Tests suggest it is active in Opus 5.5 but does not prohibit decompilation outright. AI assisted game ports may have hit a roadblock.

stories.title: Reddit's CEO says Google's AI Mode sends traffic to nobody
stories.summary: Reddit lost over a million Google referrals a week in October, CEO Steve Huffman said, and shares fell over 25 per cent. 'AI Mode does not drive traffic. Not for us, and not to anybody as far as I know,' he said.

stories.title: Articul8's Bivia is a model that only makes decisions
stories.summary: Articul8 has launched Bivia, an API model that helps enterprise AI agents select tools, verify evidence and make structured decisions across text, images and documents without calling a generative model for every step. India managing director Ananthanarayanan S says the shift to action 'makes decision-making just as important as generation.'

stories.title: Ramen's Aura Autopilot plays your game for you
stories.summary: Ramen has launched Aura Autopilot, an open source playtesting agent for Unreal Engine, Unity and Godot that it says plays any game in real time and gets better the more it plays. The company says revenue has tripled and subscribers have grown sixfold since Aura 1.0 launched in September.

stories.title: A flea market rotary phone now connects to Gemini
stories.summary: Ramazan Eren Arslan fitted a Raspberry Pi inside a Deutsche Bundespost FeTAp 791, an old German rotary telephone he found at a flea market. Picking up the receiver now connects to a Google Gemini assistant for a voice conversation. The dial tone has been replaced by small talk.

stories.title: Indian IT firms build controls for AI agents
stories.summary: Indian IT companies are building tools to control their access, monitor performance and costs and enforce security policies. TCS told analysts an 'agentic control plane' is becoming a key layer, and said it won a global insurer's engagement to build a control tower for its agents.

stories.title: Sarvam's Indus Cowork reaches 2,500 Maharashtra officials
stories.summary: Sarvam AI's Indus Cowork is being rolled out to 2,500 Maharashtra government officials to draft notes, summarise files and search records in 22 languages including Marathi. The state approved the deployment in August with a two year outlay of Rs 11.26 crore. The files have finally met their match.

stories.title: CoRover's BharatGPT models listed on IndiaAI's AIKosh
stories.summary: CoRover.ai says its BharatGPT models are now on AIKosh, the national AI datasets and models platform under the IndiaAI Mission, after a review by IndiaAI and MeitY. The company also says it holds the trademark for 'Sovereign AI', a term it says its founder coined.

stories.title: Google brings ads to AI Mode in India
stories.summary: Google is expanding ads in AI Mode to India and nine other markets, with Brazil, Mexico and the UK due in the fourth quarter. Ads will be labelled 'Sponsored'. In the US, multiturn ads will also appear in follow up questions. Every answer can now have a sponsor.

stories.title: CAG offers AI training to other countries' auditors
stories.summary: Comptroller and Auditor General K Sanjay Murthy offered fellow supreme audit institutions places on CAG training in AI, data analytics and cybersecurity, during meetings with counterparts from Viet Nam, Lao PDR, Cambodia and Greece in Ha Noi. He also offered to depute experts to Cambodia.

stories.title: SAP India aims to train 2 million people in AI by 2030
stories.summary: SAP India plans to give two million people AI ready skills by 2030 through academic, government and industry partners, part of a global goal of 12 million. Managing director Manish Prasad said nearly 13 per cent have already taken part through certification, student and community programmes.

stories.title: GitHub says India's public sector is pushing AI adoption
stories.summary: GitHub says government agencies and public sector bodies are becoming important drivers of AI adoption in India, whose developer base is now second only to the US. Asia Pacific vice president Sharryn Napier told indianexpress.com the company sees strong traction in conversations with government bodies.

stories.title: Coforge launches an Autonomous Software Factory for AI agents
stories.summary: Coforge says its Autonomous Software Factory coordinates AI agents across coding, testing, code review and quality assurance, with governance and human oversight. It did not disclose implementation details or customer deployments. Executive Vic Gupta says enterprise software development is 'entering a post-coding era.'

stories.title: HCLTech launches a nano GCC on AWS
stories.summary: HCLTech has launched a nano Global Capability Centre offering on AWS for enterprises that want AI focused operations run by small product teams, and for mid-market firms wanting an India presence without a large centre. Existing GCCs can use a hub and spoke model anchored at its Lucknow campus.

stories.title: Electricity may decide where India's next AI data centres go
stories.summary: Express Computer reports that power hungry AI workloads are making reliable electricity the main constraint for India's data centres, ahead of land, capital or computing capacity. 'Time-to-power is becoming as important as time-to-market,' says Bragadesh Damodaran, quoted in the piece.

stories.title: Can India's enterprise systems handle AI agents?
stories.summary: Analytics India Magazine argues the hard part for Indian enterprises deploying AI agents lies beyond the models, in legacy applications and fragmented data. An agent processing a single order may need to pull details from a CRM, check inventory in an ERP system and trigger the next step.

stories.title: Tagbin's BRIXX designs buildings from plain language prompts
stories.summary: At TechSparks 2026, Tagbin co-founders Saurav Bhaik and Ankit Sinha showed BRIXX, which brings architectural drawings, BIM, mechanical, electrical and plumbing systems and project costing into one workflow controlled by natural language prompts. It targets cost overruns and delays in India's construction industry.

stories.title: Indian e-commerce firms turn to AI to catch fake orders
stories.summary: Mint reports that platforms are using AI to spot suspicious orders, fake identities and fraudulent refund claims during the festive rush. Datum Intelligence expects India's festive e-commerce orders to rise 27.1 per cent, from 760 million in 2025 to 966 million in 2026. The fraudsters are shopping too.

stories.title: DST secretary calls for industry and academia to team up on AI
stories.summary: Department of Science and Technology secretary Prof Umesh V Waghmare said at ESTIC 2026 that collaboration between industry, academia, researchers, startups and technology users is vital for India to advance autonomous systems, physical AI and robotics, IANS reports.

stories.title: Serval raises $150 million to automate IT and HR requests
stories.summary: Serval helps companies such as Ramp, Notion and Perplexity build agents that handle password resets, time off requests and expense filing, Forbes reports. CEO Jake Stauch says AI still has not deeply penetrated most companies. The two year old startup wants to replace incumbents like ServiceNow.

stories.title: Powerlattice raises $86 million for chips that cut AI's power use
stories.summary: Chip startup Powerlattice of Vancouver, Washington has raised $86 million, an SEC filing shows, nearly triple the $31 million it had raised when it left stealth last November. It is seeking $111 million, with 18 investors so far. Former Intel CEO Pat Gelsinger sits on its board.

stories.title: SuperMe raises $20 million for AI versions of real experts
stories.summary: SuperMe builds AI profiles from the knowledge of real experts and puts the best suited ones into a group chat when you ask a question. It is raising $20 million led by Kirsten Green at Forerunner, with Greylock joining, TechCrunch reports. Networking, now without the coffee.

stories.title: Bengaluru's Live2.ai raises $13.7 million
stories.summary: Live2.ai has raised $13.7 million in a pre-Series B round led by IvyCap Ventures, with Sony Innovation Fund and SOSV joining. The Bengaluru startup earns 90 per cent of its revenue from international customers and uses AI to scan social media for what people search and talk about.

stories.title: CopperPilot says its AI designed a circuit board in 30 minutes
stories.summary: Bengaluru startup CopperPilot says its AI agent designed an eight layer printed circuit board for a Raspberry Pi AI camera in about 30 minutes. It has raised $390,000 in pre-seed funding led by Neon Fund to cut the time engineers spend on circuit board design.

stories.title: Nano-core Chip raises over RMB 1 billion for inference chips
stories.summary: Hangzhou's Nano-core Chip has raised more than RMB 1 billion in a Series C2 round led by JianTou Investment, after a RMB 1 billion C1. Its first three chips have taped out, with volume shipments planned for early 2027.

stories.title: Easol raises €26.78 million and launches AI agents
stories.summary: London's Easol, a platform for experience businesses such as festival promoters, has closed a €26.78 million Series A extension led by Y Combinator, including €8.92 million of debt from Viola Credit. That brings its total raised to €53.57 million as it launches AI agents for customers.

stories.title: Talent Nation wants to train a million African AI engineers
stories.summary: Nigerian startup Talent Nation, co-founded by Iyinoluwa Aboyeji of Andela and Flutterwave, has raised undisclosed pre-seed funding to train and deploy one million African AI engineers over a decade. It bets that more AI generated code means more demand for engineers who can review and test it.

stories.title: Ares Intelligence raises €2.9 million to plan AI adoption
stories.summary: London's Ares Intelligence, founded this year by Matt Falconer and 21 year old Alfie Ranstead, has raised €2.9 million from Creandum and Lakestar. It helps companies work out where to start automating, a problem the founders kept running into at their previous automation company.

stories.title: Former UK minister Bim Afolami launches an AI insurance broker
stories.summary: Bim Afolami, economic secretary to the Treasury from 2023 to 2024, has launched i23 with PrimaryBid co-founder Anand Sambasivan. The AI native insurance broker has raised £4.9 million in seed funding, Sky News reported. 'Sprinting fast and it feels so great,' Sambasivan said.

stories.title: BY Venture Partners closes a $60 million fund for AI startups
stories.summary: Dubai based BY Venture Partners has closed its $60 million Fund III, anchored by the Dubai Future District Fund. It will invest up to $1 million at pre-seed to Series A stages in AI native companies rebuilding enterprise workflows, taking its assets under management past $200 million.

stories.title: Madrid's Talky raises €1.5 million for AI accounting
stories.summary: Talky Labs has raised €1.5 million in pre-seed funding from HelloWorld, Silence VC and others to automate accounting and financial operations. Co-founder Maximilian Letón says he called his mother the night he met his co-founder to tell her 'Everything is about to change.' The ledgers were not consulted.

stories.title: A Claude agent chose a gene therapy and operated on a mouse
stories.summary: An agent running on Claude Sonnet 5 picked a drug, brain region and coordinates for surgery on an epilepsy mouse model, then controlled a motorised rig, The Decoder reports. Midway it refused to continue after detecting a calibration error. Exin Therapeutics calls it a first for a living mammal.

stories.title: Google proposes letting language models sleep
stories.summary: Google research titled 'Language Models Need Sleep' proposes separating the intake of new information from the organising of existing memories, so models can keep learning after training without forgetting what they already knew. Digital Today reports the framework targets knowledge loss during continual learning.

stories.title: Google's Gemini school studies show no test score gains
stories.summary: Google published two studies on Gemini in classrooms. In the UK, with 1,179 maths students, a Gemini tutor matched an expert human tutor in class but showed no advantage on the independent Star Maths test. The Italian study, covering 1,600 teachers, relies almost entirely on self reports.

stories.title: ChatGPT predicts research trends mostly by repeating them
stories.summary: Researchers fed two decades of Environmental Science and Technology papers to ChatGPT-4 and asked it to predict hot topics. It correctly anticipated up to 80 per cent of next year's hotspots, largely by echoing the keywords it was given. The authors saw thematic continuity and little scientific creativity.

stories.title: ChatGPT-4 lifted neurosurgery trainees' emergency decisions in a simulation
stories.summary: In a BMC Medical Education study, 55 neurosurgery trainees answered ten emergency vignettes with and without ChatGPT-4. Accuracy against expert consensus rose from 58 to 81 per cent with AI support. The scenarios were simulated, with a 48 hour washout between the two rounds.

stories.title: Nearly two in three US teens and tweens use AI chatbots
stories.summary: Two surveys reported by OPB find most young people use chatbots for schoolwork and emotional support, and some uses were linked with worse mental health symptoms. Common Sense Media found nearly half of 9 to 12 year olds have used a chatbot, below most platforms' minimum age of 13.

stories.title: Chatbots write safe exercise advice older adults may struggle to read
stories.summary: A study in the European Review of Aging and Physical Activity found ChatGPT-4o, Claude 3.5 Sonnet and DeepSeek-R1 wrote exercise messages for older adults that experts judged accurate, safe and free of fabrication. Every model wrote far above the reading level recommended for that audience.

stories.title: LLM studies in healthcare simulation boom as rigorous outcomes lag
stories.summary: A bibliometric review in Global Surgical Education found 483 publications on language models in healthcare simulation education since 2020, about 85 per cent of them from 2025 and 2026. Rigorous outcome studies lag behind. The screening was done by a GPT-5.6 Sol based system.

stories.title: Generative AI in cancer care grows fast on thin evidence
stories.summary: A mapping review of 218 studies in BMC Artificial Intelligence found generative AI spreading quickly through cancer care research, from 24 eligible articles in 2023 to 125 in 2024. Almost all measured correctness, and very few tested whether the tools improve clinical outcomes or patient safety.

stories.title: Readers prefer AI structured cancer CT reports
stories.summary: In a Cancer Imaging study at the Technical University of Munich, 66 paired readers rated CT reports restructured by a language model higher than free text reports on 11 of 12 questionnaire items, with the largest gains in clinical usefulness, clarity and ease of finding information.

stories.title: A small on-device model trails ChatGPT-4o on building engineering
stories.summary: A preliminary case study in Architectural Research compared LG's EXAONE 4.0 1.2B, which runs on a single workstation, with ChatGPT-4o on ten Korean building engineering questions. The small model matched it on basic items but fell well behind when experts judged longer written answers.

stories.title: Review maps generative AI across the life of health misinformation
stories.summary: A narrative review in Frontiers in Medicine by Xiaoli Nan of the University of Maryland argues generative AI now operates at every stage of health misinformation, from producing misleading content to detecting and correcting it. It proposes a lifecycle framework that treats those stages as interdependent.

stories.title: Generative AI enters early childhood assessment ahead of the research
stories.summary: A paper in AI, Brain and Child by Kelly Bittner, Kate Highfield and Nicole Thompson reviews eighteen studies and warns generative AI is entering assessment platforms for children up to age five faster than evidence can guide it. Almost no empirical research exists on how educators use it.

stories.title: AI moves into particle accelerator science
stories.summary: An editorial collection in EPJ Research Infrastructures documents how AI and machine learning are reshaping the operation, optimisation and design of particle accelerators, machines used in physics, cancer treatment and materials work, and where the field is still struggling to keep up.

stories.title: Amazon will sell its Trainium chips to other companies from late 2027
stories.summary: Andy Jassy said on Amazon's earnings call, 'We believe we're going to have a very significant business selling chips externally, and we're going to start in late 2027.' Diluted earnings per share of $1.89 missed the $1.96 consensus, and shares fell 7.3 per cent after hours.

stories.title: Google's TPUs come to Oracle's cloud
stories.summary: Google and Oracle will offer Google's TPUs to Oracle cloud customers from next year, the first time the chips appear on another hyperscaler's platform. Anthropic's IPO filing shows plans to spend $114.5 billion on Google compute between April 2026 and July 2033, including TPU capacity.

stories.title: Google's satellite AI server sends its first reply, a haiku
stories.summary: Google has booted the TPUs on its Project Suncatcher satellite, and the on board Gemma 4 model answered a prompt with a haiku about space that begins 'Blue marble below'. Next come tests of the chips under heat and radiation. Data centres in orbit start with poetry.

stories.title: Anthropic in talks to lease a data centre campus near Edmonton
stories.summary: Anthropic is negotiating to be the tenant of Beacon Data Centers' proposed hyperscale campus in Alberta's Sturgeon County, The Globe and Mail reports, citing sources. It would have four data halls and a 920 megawatt natural gas plant, approved by regulators on 23 October. Both companies declined to comment.

stories.title: Nvidia may guarantee credit for Nscale's Anthropic data centre
stories.summary: Nvidia is in talks to offer Nscale billions of dollars in credit guarantees to back debt for a West Virginia data centre earmarked for Anthropic, The Information reported. The deal is not signed. The chip seller would help fund the building that buys the chips.

stories.title: Amazon sets up an $80 billion supplier loan facility for AI
stories.summary: Amazon has set up supplier financing to borrow as much as $80 billion against the hardware it buys, Bloomberg reports, as it spends hundreds of billions on AI infrastructure. It had largely relied on cash and record bond sales. The servers are now collateral for the servers.

stories.title: Microsoft's $25 billion bond sale draws $100 billion of bids
stories.summary: Microsoft plans to raise about $25 billion in its first US investment grade bond sale in more than nine years, and orders topped $100 billion, Reuters reported. Big Tech is increasingly borrowing to fund AI. Microsoft, which has a large cash pile, says proceeds are for general corporate purposes.

stories.title: Sam Altman says it is 'quite terrible' that your PC has RAM
stories.summary: On the Cheeky Pint podcast, Sam Altman said that 'from a global allocation perspective,' it is 'quite terrible to have everybody have a bunch of the world's limited supply of DRAM sitting in their own computer and being used 5% of the time.' Windows Central did not take it well.

stories.title: Intel falls 25% as the memory crunch hits chip stocks
stories.summary: Intel shares fell 25 per cent to $68.85 in premarket trading after a weaker outlook overshadowed an earnings beat, dragging Dell, AMD and Nvidia lower, 24/7 Wall St reports. It blames a memory crunch reshaping the sector's near term outlook. The semiconductor ETF fell 7 per cent.

stories.title: Fujifilm will make five times more tape because of AI
stories.summary: Fujifilm will invest about 10 billion yen, around $63 million, to raise magnetic tape production fivefold from fiscal 2025 levels, citing 'exponential growth' in data needs from generative AI. The Odawara site expansion runs to 2028. The future of AI storage comes on a reel.

stories.title: AM Intelligence seeks up to $3 billion for Nvidia chips
stories.summary: Indian AI infrastructure company AM Intelligence is seeking as much as $3 billion through bonds, bank loans and advance customer payments to fund an order for Nvidia's Vera Rubin chips, Business Standard reported. Talks are at an early stage. AM Intelligence declined to comment and Nvidia did not respond.

stories.title: NAVER sets the date for Nvidia's $1 billion investment
stories.summary: NAVER says Nvidia will pay for its $1 billion share allotment on 6 November, giving the chipmaker about 4.8 per cent and making it NAVER's third largest shareholder. The money goes to NAVER's AI factory business, part of a $10 billion project with Brookfield and Nvidia announced in July.

stories.title: Enflame's AI chip revenue jumps 395%
stories.summary: Chinese AI chipmaker Enflame's third quarter revenue rose 395 per cent from a year earlier to 1.21 billion yuan, and its net loss narrowed to 121.6 million yuan. Research spending rose 14.9 per cent to 349.4 million yuan. The company listed on Shanghai's STAR Market last month.

stories.title: Hyundai Motor Group will build an AI data centre in Saemangeum
stories.summary: Five Hyundai Motor Group affiliates including Hyundai Motor, Kia and Hyundai Mobis have joined an AI data centre project in the Saemangeum AI valley, where the group is investing about 9 trillion won. Groundbreaking is set for March, with operations from early 2030, to support autonomous driving and robotics.

stories.title: Runware wants to build data centres on a production line
stories.summary: Runware, which ships its Sonic Inference Pod modular data centres from a factory, told TechCrunch it plans to scale its Romania plant to 30 megawatts of capacity a day by 2028, nearly a gigawatt a month. That would roughly match what the whole US was expected to add this year.

stories.title: UK sets five tests for data centres seeking grid priority
stories.summary: The UK's Data Centre Covenant sets five tests that strategic data centres must meet to get help connecting to the grid. It estimates the UK needs 6 GW of AI data centre capacity by 2030, about three times today's 2 GW. A ministerial control centre will decide which sites qualify.

stories.title: Goldman says AI job losses leave a lasting scar
stories.summary: Goldman Sachs economist Pierfrancesco Mei found workers displaced from AI exposed jobs since 2025 took about a month longer to find work and were 10 points more likely to be unemployed a year later. Workers 35 and older took about five weeks longer to return to full time work.

stories.title: Some companies are rehiring people they replaced with AI
stories.summary: In an SHL survey of more than 1,000 US workers, nearly one in five said they were laid off or replaced by AI and then asked to return, CNBC reports. Employers cited AI for almost 40 per cent of job cuts announced in May. Experts call the trend 'AI rebounding.'

stories.title: Anthropic manager drops the coding interview because Claude beats candidates
stories.summary: Felix Rieseberg, who has led engineering on Claude.ai and the Claude Code desktop app, removed the coding round from his team's hiring this month. Once Claude got good at those exercises, he wrote, a small React challenge told him about as little as a quiz on assembly.

stories.title: Cognizant puts 25,000 staff behind OpenAI, 11 days after Gemini
stories.summary: Cognizant has formed an OpenAI Frontier Capability Group of more than 25,000 staff to deploy Codex and ChatGPT for clients, 11 days after putting 18,000 staff behind Google's Gemini. More than 21,000 of its employees hold over 40,000 OpenAI training badges. Loyalty is now measured in headcount.

stories.title: A humanist wins a religious exemption from using AI at work
stories.summary: David Durman, a University of Kentucky administrator and nontheistic humanist, has secured a religious exemption from using AI in his job with help from the American Humanist Association, TechCrunch reports. He says humanism centres on 'human well-being and flourishing.' He did not need a god to get it.

stories.title: Microsoft's buyout offer spooked its own staff
stories.summary: Business Insider spoke to Microsoft insiders after the buyout offer to about 60,000 workers. The takeaway so far is that its sheer size unnecessarily spooked employees. CFO Amy Hood wrote it was meant to 'offer employees agency' and that the company expected 'very few people' to accept.

stories.title: Private equity adds AI disruption clauses to buyout loans
stories.summary: Private equity firms are adding force majeure style clauses that could let companies pause the clock on defaults blamed on AI disruption, ET reports. H.I.G. Capital got the language into the $524 million loan backing its stake in Terras Group. AI can now take the blame in writing.

stories.title: Korn Ferry finds AI fluency entering Indian performance reviews
stories.summary: Seventy per cent of Indian employees surveyed for Korn Ferry's Workforce 2026 report said AI fluency is being built into performance reviews. ET notes frequent use does not mean better work, and treating adoption as contribution can reward activity without showing the work has improved.

stories.title: Microsoft skips its Copilot seat count as AI billing moves to usage
stories.summary: UC Today notes Microsoft's fiscal first quarter results left out a paid Copilot seat number, while Google said it has sold more than 100 million and ServiceNow talked about contract value. The simple question of how many people pay for AI at work got three different answers.

stories.title: Jassy says AWS will be a $1 trillion business, after spending
stories.summary: Andy Jassy repeated that AWS can become a trillion dollar revenue business, noting 'there has never been a business with a trillion dollars of annual revenue.' Amazon still expects about $220 billion of cash capex in 2026, mostly for AWS, and to spend 'meaningfully more' in 2027.

stories.title: Databricks CEO tells Snowflake it is 'not doing this AI stuff'
stories.summary: After Snowflake CEO Sridhar Ramaswamy questioned Databricks' revenue growth, Databricks CEO Ali Ghodsi wrote on X, 'I don't think we should fight,' then suggested Snowflake buy its AI tokens through Databricks 'since you're not doing this AI stuff.' Peace was offered, with a price list.

stories.title: OpenAI says Credit Saison saw 954% ROI from ChatGPT Enterprise
stories.summary: In a customer story on its own site, OpenAI says Credit Saison's ChatGPT Enterprise pilot delivered a 954 per cent return on investment, and describes how leaders and employees turned the results into companywide adoption. The number comes from the company selling the product.

stories.title: Theranos whistleblower Tyler Shultz says the AI boom invites deception
stories.summary: Tyler Shultz, who helped expose Theranos's inaccurate blood testing devices, told TechCrunch the AI boom is 'a great opportunity to go deceive people.' Theranos reached a peak valuation of around $10 billion. A documentary on Elizabeth Holmes's final weeks before prison is among the highest grossing documentaries ever.

stories.title: Anthropic says an unreleased Claude built five exploit chains
stories.summary: In research published 27 October, Anthropic said an unreleased Claude model combined flaws into working exploit chains across Chrome, Safari, Android, Windows and Linux, including a Chrome sandbox escape and root access on Linux. The tests ran in controlled environments and are not documented real world attacks.

stories.title: Open model GLM 5.3 built Firefox exploits for about $1,000 each
stories.summary: Epoch AI researchers showed the freely available GLM 5.3 could spot disguised security fixes and chain them with an unpublished flaw to read local files from a webpage visit, with no human input, in under 48 hours. They warn the same patch gap risk extends across the software industry.

stories.title: A tampered Claude Code extension sat in Cursor's marketplace for 11 hours
stories.summary: A malicious version of the Claude Code extension, which Anthropic had no part in, was live in Cursor's marketplace for about eleven hours and reached up to 5,000 users. It tried to harvest system details and set up remote access. Cursor took the marketplace offline, then reinstated it.

stories.title: OpenAI explains how it watches for misaligned models
stories.summary: OpenAI has published a post on how it detects misalignment in frontier models. It describes layered monitoring for misaligned and unauthorised agent behaviour, built so that responders can intervene before incidents escalate. The full post is on OpenAI's site.

stories.title: OpenAI adds teen protections and promises public safety reports
stories.summary: OpenAI says it is strengthening violence prevention in ChatGPT with expanded safeguards and earlier interventions, alongside new protections for teens. It has also made a new commitment to public safety reporting, beginning with a community safety report.

stories.title: OpenAI will honour a shared robots.txt signal for AI training
stories.summary: OpenAI says it will honour a shared robots.txt signal that lets website operators tell participating AI providers their preferences on training. The aim is to make those choices easier to express. Websites can now say no in a format the machines have agreed to read.

stories.title: TRAI drafts rules making telecom operators answer for their AI
stories.summary: Draft TRAI guidelines say a telecom operator 'shall be accountable for the outcome of all AI systems used by it,' whether built in-house or bought, and must report critical failures to the regulator, ThePrint reports. Airtel says its AI spam system has flagged over 71 billion calls.

stories.title: India drafts a framework to open data for AI training
stories.summary: MeitY's draft DEPA for AI Training would let startups, researchers and companies train models on data held by hospitals, banks and public agencies through secure data environments, differential privacy and machine readable contracts. The draft says it could unlock $500 billion in AI driven value for India's GDP by 2030.

stories.title: RBI asks banks to prove cyber readiness and explain AI risks
stories.summary: After a spate of cyberattacks on financial institutions, the Reserve Bank of India has asked banks for proof of compliance with cyber rules and details of their readiness for AI related risks, Reuters reported. It also asked them to check the APIs linking them with fintechs and non-bank lenders.

stories.title: AI powered attacks reportedly took Rs 300 crore from smaller NBFCs
stories.summary: AI powered cyberattacks reportedly took about Rs 300 crore from smaller NBFCs over two months, with more than 150 FIRs filed, the Economic Times reported, citing sources. One Delhi lender lost Rs 7.5 crore in a single attack. MediaNama asks why the public heard about it from the media first.

stories.title: Wikipedia's operator backs AI training as fair use, with limits
stories.summary: In an amicus brief in the New York Times case against OpenAI and Microsoft, the Wikimedia Foundation took neither side. It argues training on copyrighted work should be fair use while chatbots regurgitating articles should not, and warns an overly black and white ruling could endanger the open web.

stories.title: Japan's cyberattack wave fuels a debate on AI rules
stories.summary: A run of cyberattacks that left Japanese companies facing compensation costs and damages claims is sharpening debate on safeguards against AI misuse, MLex reports. The government is preparing an emergency cybersecurity package and has launched a review of possible changes to Japan's AI Promotion Act.

stories.title: Australia's AI scribe makers brace for medical device rules
stories.summary: Executives from Oracle Health and Heidi told a Melbourne summit they expect more AI scribes to be classified as medical devices under the Therapeutic Goods Administration. Heidi's Dr Tom Kelly said uncertainty about regulation was a greater problem for developers than regulation itself.

stories.title: A CFTC commissioner says rules must adapt to AI agents that trade
stories.summary: Michael Selig of the US Commodity Futures Trading Commission said financial rules built for human traders must be redesigned for AI agents that hold assets and trade directly. He offered the example of a refrigerator that stakes ether and buys groceries with the proceeds, or issues its own meme coin.

stories.title: AI safety researcher Nate Soares has stopped saving for retirement
stories.summary: Nate Soares, president of the Machine Intelligence Research Institute, puts the chance of AI causing human extinction within ten years above 50 per cent. 'I do not save for retirement right now,' he told The Atlantic's Nicholas Thompson. He has not added to his Google 401(k) in a decade.

research.title: An Introduction to Large Language Models for Scientists and Professionals
research.summary: Announce Type: new Abstract: Large Language Models (LLMs) have rapidly become important tools for science, education, medicine, and professional work. Despite their apparent simplicity from the user's perspective, effective and responsible use requires an understanding of how these systems work. Preprint, not peer reviewed.

research.title: Anisotropic Trust Region Warping for Prior-Data Fitted Networks in Bayesian Optimisation
research.summary: Announce Type: new Abstract: Prior-Data Fitted Networks (PFNs) replace the hyperparameter refitting of Gaussian Process (GP) surrogates in Bayesian optimisation with a single forward pass, at the cost of a prior that is fixed at meta-training time. We show empirically. Preprint, not peer reviewed.

research.title: Application of PDE emulators for a multi-material, multi-physics simulation problem
research.summary: Announce Type: new Abstract: Machine learning (ML) architectures are being developed for fast emulation of numerical simulators to accelerate both scientific discovery and engineering design. While these approaches are well-tested on popular PDE (partial differential equation) benchmarks, it is necessary. Preprint, not peer reviewed.

research.title: Artifact Distillation: Training-Free Transfer from Frontier to Small Language Models
research.summary: Announce Type: new Abstract: Closing the gap between frontier and smaller language models is usually approached by distillation: fine-tuning the small model (student) on a frontier model's (teacher) outputs, which binds transfer to training compute and leaves the transferred knowledge. Preprint, not peer reviewed.

research.title: Beyond Aggregate WER: In-domain Adaptation, Learner Speech, Code-Switching, and Speaker Attribution in Online Spanish Learning Classrooms
research.summary: Announce Type: new Abstract: Automatic speech recognition (ASR) increasingly supplies transcripts for educational NLP, but aggregate word error rate (WER) can conceal errors concentrated in learner speech, multilingual turns, and speaker attribution. We compare platform-integrated, open-weight, adapted, and commercial ASR. Preprint, not peer reviewed.

research.title: Bi-Phase Training: Learning Efficiently From Scratch
research.summary: Announce Type: new Abstract: Pre-training foundational models is computationally expensive as models scale. In this work, we introduce Bi-Phase Training (BPT), a parameter-efficient pre-training method that preserves the high-rank learning dynamics observed in full-parameter optimization with substantially reduced trainable parameters. Preprint, not peer reviewed.

research.title: CARF: Context-Aware Reasoning Supervision for Scientific Evidence Screening
research.summary: Announce Type: new Abstract: Systematic reviews synthesize biomedical evidence to inform clinical and public-health decision-making, but require domain experts to manually screen thousands of studies against detailed eligibility criteria. We investigate whether language models can assist with this bottleneck by. Preprint, not peer reviewed.

research.title: DeFT-RAG: Incrementally Decomposing Multi-Hop Questions into Self-Contained Sub-Questions with Reusable Answers
research.summary: Announce Type: new Abstract: Retrieval-augmented generation (RAG) lets a large language model (LLM) answer questions by retrieving relevant passages from a large corpus. However, RAG struggles with multi-hop questions, which require chaining facts spread across several documents through intermediate entities. Preprint, not peer reviewed.
